title: Ines and the Autopsy Revisited
premise: Estate lawyer Oscar Sandoval has spent three years burying the town of Marrow Creek's secrets beneath meticulous paperwork, including the suspicious autopsy that closed the case of heiress Vivian Ashcombe's death. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to the murder, one promising the truth is still alive—Oscar realizes the will he probated was forged and the witness everyone swears is dead may be hiding in plain sight. As a retrial looms, Oscar must choose between protecting his own complicity in the cover-up and exposing the town's most powerful family. In the end, he finds the 'dead' witness—Vivian herself, disfigured and erased by her own family—and testifies against them, surrendering his law license but reclaiming his name.
about_author: J. M. Dravenmoor spent a decade as a paralegal in small-town probate courts before turning to fiction, where the dead speak through paperwork. A recluse of undisclosed location, Dravenmoor writes only at night and answers no interviews.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Oscar Sandoval. Three years after probating Vivian Ashcombe's estate, Oscar receives a second will dated after the first—impossible, since she's dead. His hands shake as he files it away out of habit. The beat: dread disguised as routine, the moment invisibility starts to crack.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Two envelopes arrive the same morning: one signed by Vivian's brother Cassius confessing to her murder, one unsigned promising 'the witness is warmer than her grave.' Oscar burns neither. The beat: paralysis—the lawyer who files everything suddenly can't file anything.

chapters.title: Marrow Creek Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Oscar touring town: the diner where everyone praises the Ashcombes, the courthouse where the autopsy was sealed by Judge Pell, himself an Ashcombe cousin. Everyone swears the sole witness, groundskeeper Tomás Iriarte, died in 2019. The beat: suffocating consensus.

chapters.title: Cassius in the Dock
chapters.summary: POV Oscar at the county jail, where Cassius recants his confession within minutes, smiling, saying someone wants him to hang for a crime the whole family committed together. He hints Oscar already knows why. The beat: the confession as bait, not truth.

chapters.title: The Alphabetized Dead
chapters.summary: POV Oscar ransacking his own filing cabinets at night, finding the gaps he built into Vivian's estate file on purpose—pages he removed to protect someone he loved. The beat: self-reckoning; the archivist discovers he is the archive's biggest lie.

chapters.title: What Dolores Kept
chapters.summary: POV Dolores Vann, Oscar's secretary, who reveals she photocopied the missing pages years ago and has been waiting for him to ask. She gives him the original autopsy: cause of death rewritten from drowning to heart failure. The beat: unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: A Grave With No Tenant
chapters.summary: POV Oscar exhumes records showing Tomás Iriarte's death certificate was signed by a doctor who left the state before the date on it. Someone paid for a paper corpse. The beat: hope sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Table
chapters.summary: POV Oscar summoned to dinner at Ashcombe Hall by matriarch Regina, who offers him a partnership, a house, and silence, all while carving meat with terrible precision. She knows about the letters. The beat: power extended like a blade handle-first.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Dolores. Oscar's office is broken into overnight; the second will is gone, and a disciplinary complaint appears against him with the state bar. Dolores hides the photocopies inside hymnals at her church. The beat: the machinery of corruption grinding personal.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Cottage
chapters.summary: POV Oscar searching the abandoned cottage on Ashcombe land, finding a woman's clothing in Tomás's size, medicine bottles, and fresh footprints. Someone lives there—or did until very recently. The beat: the dead witness leaving warmth behind.

chapters.title: Regina's Version
chapters.summary: POV Regina Ashcombe. Her chapter reframes everything: Vivian was the corrupt one, blackmailing the family, and Tomás was her accomplice. Regina believes she saved the town. The beat: villainy with a fully lit interior; power as sincere delusion.

chapters.title: Judge Pell's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Oscar confronting the retired judge over brandy, extracting how the autopsy was sealed: Regina holds evidence of Pell's own buried crime. Everyone in Marrow Creek is held by a thread. The beat: complicity as currency.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. A third letter arrives, this one in Vivian's handwriting, describing the night of her 'death' in detail only she could know—and naming Oscar as the lawyer who helped forge the first will. The beat: betrayal; his protection was participation.

chapters.title: Dolores Disappears
chapters.summary: POV Oscar. Dolores misses work for the first time in nineteen years; her apartment is stripped, hymnals included. The church organist mentions a tall woman in a scarf asking for her. The beat: fear for the innocent, guilt doubling.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: POV Oscar learns the retrial of Cassius is calendared in eleven days—with Oscar subpoenaed as the estate's expert witness, forced to swear to documents he knows are forged. The beat: the trap closing on its designer.

chapters.title: Warmth Under the Floor
chapters.summary: POV Oscar returns to the cottage at night and finds a trapdoor cellar: living space, books, and a mirror cracked across the middle. On the wall, a timeline of his own filings. He has been watched for three years. The beat: hunter realizing he was also prey.

chapters.title: Vivian
chapters.summary: POV Vivian Ashcombe. She reveals herself: scarred from the staged drowning, hidden by Tomás, now dying slowly and choosing to end the silence. She doesn't want revenge—she wants her name back on her own life. The beat: the witness everyone swore was dead, alive and resolute.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: POV Oscar preparing testimony with Vivian in hiding, dodging bar investigators, discovering Dolores is safe—Vivian's people took her in. Regina offers Oscar one final deal: destroy the letters or lose everything. The beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, courtroom climax. He takes the stand, recants his expert opinion, and calls Vivian Ashcombe to testify—alive, veiled, voice steady. The courtroom detonates; Judge Pell tries to gavel it down and fails. The beat: catharsis through public truth.

chapters.title: What the Family Buried
chapters.summary: POV Vivian. Her testimony unspools the full conspiracy: the forged will, the bought coroner, the erased witness. Cassius walks free; Regina is arrested mid-sneer; Pell resigns rather than face impeachment. The beat: justice arriving loud and imperfect.

chapters.title: Surrender of License
chapters.summary: POV Oscar voluntarily surrenders his law license, disbarred for the forgery he once committed, and finds the loss lighter than expected. Dolores returns to work—for Vivian, who is reopening the estate honestly. The beat: identity rebuilt without the armor.

chapters.title: Ines and the Autopsy Revisited
chapters.summary: POV Oscar, epilogue. He learns the title's meaning: 'Ines' was the alias Vivian used in hiding, and the autopsy she revisited was her own. Standing at her recovered grave marker—her real name restored—he finally files nothing, keeps nothing, and stays visible. The beat: quiet peace earned through ruin.
